label: High at D1 after reward; at D2 higher after choosing a2 and when S2 believed good.
terms: (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 1) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 1) * (prev_action == 2) ;; (phase == D1) * belief_lo ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 2) ;; (phase == D2) * belief_lo ;; (phase == D2) * (state == 2) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 2) ;; (phase == D1) * (tv("reward", -2) == 1)
explanation: Raw reset gate r of unit 22; timing (high at D1, low at GO, mid at D2) explains R^2 0.77. Beyond timing: at D1 it rises strongly when the previous trial was rewarded (about +0.13) and drops after no reward; at D2 it is higher when the agent just chose a2 (+0.10); at D1 and D2 it rises with the ideal-observer belief that S2 is good (negative weight on belief_lo). GO is nearly flat. The free fit adds a bigger reward boost after a2 choices, a negative prev_state==S2 term at D1, the reached state at D2 and the reward two trials back (dev 0.69 vs short 0.63). No future variables or model outputs used.

issues: The belief term has the wrong shape. Replacing belief_lo with belief (the probability itself) in the same 3-term short form raises test R^2 beyond timing from 0.623 to 0.758 (dev 0.768). That is above the reported free fit of 0.68. The gate tracks the saturating probability, not the unbounded log-odds; np.tanh(belief_lo) scores 0.621 and (belief_lo > 0) scores 0.724.

The label puts the belief effect in the wrong phase. It says 'at D2 ... when S2 believed good', but most of the belief effect is at D1. With belief, a D1-only term scores 0.731 on test and adding D2 brings it only to 0.758. With belief_lo, D1-only scores 0.592 and D2-only 0.560. The label never says belief matters at D1, though D1 is where it matters most once a2 is already in the D2 term.

The explanation's claim that belief acts at both D1 and D2 is weakly supported. At D2 the a2-choice term carries most of the signal. The residual table shows D2 deviations of about +/-0.09 for both choice x state and belief decile, which are confounded with each other.

A systematic error class remains in misses (worst-fit windows) for both forms: D1 after an unrewarded trial is over-predicted. Original form: a1 S1 u -0.170, a2 S1 u -0.137. Belief form: -0.135 and -0.111. The original form also under-predicts GO by about +0.045 across previous-trial patterns. A binary prev_reward boost does not fully capture how low the gate falls after no reward, especially after reaching S1.
